# Jsyxi Shipping — FINAL SPEC (build authority)

**Status:** Build authority for v1. Supersedes `brief.txt` (Jsyxi Shipping FINAL Master Document v2.0) wherever the two differ, and supersedes `_rewrites/1/spec.md` in full.
**Owner:** Mahesh Rojasara · **Product:** Jsyxi Shipping
**Domains:** dashboard `app.jsyxi.com` · APIs + courier webhooks `api.jsyxi.com` · admin `admin.jsyxi.com` · marketing `jsyxi.com`
**Generated by** `/brief-rewrite` (rewrite 2) from `brief.txt` + audit ledger `_audits/4/resolutions.md` (50 settled decisions: A1-01…A4-04 and RV-01…RV-15).

---

## 0. How to read this specification

### 0.1 Authority order

When two statements conflict, the higher row wins. This order is settled by **A1-01**.

| Rank | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | §1–§8 and §10 of this spec (the canonical reference layer) | Glossary, entities, enums, formulas, invariants, settings, contracts, permissions |
| 2 | §9 behaviour sections and §11–§13 of this spec | Must never redefine a §1–§8 concept; where a behaviour section appears to contradict the reference layer, the reference layer wins |
| 3 | The audit ledger `_audits/4/resolutions.md` | Already folded into this spec; consult only for provenance |
| 4 | `brief.txt` | Author intent; superseded on every point this spec restates |

**Appendix-wins rule:** §1–§8 and §10 are the appendices. Any term, key, enum value, formula, threshold, setting, permission or contract field is defined there exactly once. §9 references them and never restates them. If an implementer finds the same thing defined twice, the §1–§8/§10 definition is correct and the duplicate is a defect to report.

### 0.2 Sources that are NOT normative

Per **A1-01**, and confirmed at rewrite time:

- `shipping-app-features-brief.md` — **not present in the kit**. Its unstated detail is intentionally omitted. It is not a source of requirements.
- The approved Claude Design output — **not present in the kit**. It is authoritative only for visual tokens and presentation, never behaviour or data rules, and it is not available. The only design facts that survive are those stated in `brief.txt` and repeated in **§9.22**.
- The verification report on rewrite 1 is an **input to this rewrite, never a source this spec cites**. Every defect it raised was either fixed as a transcription correction or ratified into the ledger as **RV-01…RV-15** before this rewrite ran; the spec cites the ledger, not the report.
- No external link, chat log, or unavailable file is a hidden source of truth. If a requirement is not in this spec, it is not in v1.

### 0.3 Scope of this document

This spec is **stack-agnostic and UI-agnostic**: framework, coding style, component library and visual design come from the dev kit, not from here. It does state architectural requirements that affect correctness or performance, and it repeats the platform, security and compliance constraints the brief locked (§5.7).

### 0.4 Conventions

- `ENUM_VALUE` — an enum member, exactly as stored.
- `entity.field` — a field on a canonical entity from §2.
- **F-n** — a formula defined in §4. **INV-n** — a global invariant in §6. **S-n** — a configurable setting in §7. **A-n / RV-n / RW-n** — a Decision Register entry in §13.
- Money is written `₹1,234.56`. All monetary examples are INR.
- "MUST" is a requirement. "MUST NOT" is a prohibition. "Default" means a value in §7 that a merchant or admin can change.

## 1. Glossary

Every term used in this spec. Author-term → canonical-term mappings are marked **[rename]**; both labels refer to one concept.

| Canonical term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Shop** | One Shopify store that has installed Jsyxi. The tenant boundary (**INV-1**). Author terms "merchant", "store", "tenant" all map here. **[rename]** |
| **Member** | A Shopify staff user who has been granted a role on a Shop (§10). |
| **BYOC** | Bring Your Own Courier: the Shop contracts directly with each Courier and Jsyxi books on the Shop's own credentials. Jsyxi takes no freight margin, holds no balance and never touches COD cash (**INV-23**, **RV-01**). |
| **Pickup location** | The physical address goods dispatch from. Author term "warehouse" maps here. v1 allows exactly one active pickup location per Shop (**A3-01**, **A4-02**). **[rename]** |
| **Courier** | A logistics provider defined in Courier Master (e.g. Delhivery). |
| **Aggregator courier** | A Courier whose own catalogue is other couriers, reached through one API (Shiprocket at v1). Priced by live quote, not a rate card (**A2-02**). |
| **Service** | A named, bookable offering of a Courier (e.g. "DTDC B2C Priority", "Shiprocket — AMD-L039"). **Services, not Couriers, are what rules, rate cards, bookings, labels and reports operate on.** Author term "courier service" maps here. **[rename]** |
| **Courier account** | A Shop's own credentials for one Courier (BYOC). Holds `mode` = `TEST` or `LIVE` and a separate credential set for each (**A1-12**). |
| **Enabled service** | A Service the Shop has switched on for one of its Courier accounts. Only enabled services are bookable. |
| **Order** | A Shopify order mirrored into Jsyxi. Keyed by `(shop_id, shopify_order_gid)`. |
| **Order line** | One line item of an Order, mirrored with its Shopify line ID and quantity. |
| **Allocation** | The set of an Order's in-house line quantities that Jsyxi will dispatch, derived from Shopify fulfillment orders. Author term "fulfillment allocation" maps here. At v1 an Order has **one** Allocation by default (**A4-01**, **RV-11**). **[rename]** |
| **Shipment** | The unit of booking, labelling, tracking, NDR/RTO, costing and reconciliation. Exactly one parcel at v1 (**A2-12**). Holds at most one active AWB (**INV-6**). |
| **Sibling Shipment** | A second or later Shipment on the same Order. In v1 siblings arise **only** from the §9.2.3 fallback path — one Shipment per unmergeable Shopify fulfillment order. There is no merchant-initiated parcel split (**RV-06**). |
| **Shipment line** | An Order line ID + quantity carried by a Shipment. |
| **AWB** | The courier's tracking number for a Shipment. Normalized per **F-19** before any comparison or uniqueness check. |
| **Booking intent** | An immutable UUID + request digest created once per booking **attempt** and reused across every transport retry of that attempt (**A1-04**). A Shipment may accumulate several intents over its life — a retry after `FAILED`, or a rebook after a confirmed cancellation, each create a new one — but at most one is active at a time (**INV-5**). |
| **Working values** | A `DRAFT` Shipment's resolved-but-still-mutable recipient, lines, package, weights, payment mode, Collectible and (once routed) Service. Rule evaluation, the cost estimate and the ship modal all read these. They become the snapshot unchanged at `DRAFT → QUEUED` (**RV-05**). |
| **Booking snapshot** | The immutable copy of the working values frozen at `DRAFT → QUEUED` (§2.9). Everything downstream — costing, labels, reconciliation, disputes, reprints — reads it, never current master data (**INV-8**, **INV-10**). |
| **Quote** | The itemized, per-Service price and eligibility response for one Shipment (§8.3). Source is a Rate card version or a live provider call (**A2-02**). |
| **Rate card** | A Shop's contracted pricing for one Service. Immutable once used; versioned by effective-from date (**A1-05**). |
| **Rate card version** | One effective-dated version of a Rate card. The thing actually referenced by a booking snapshot. |
| **Postal zone master** | Versioned reference data mapping Indian PIN codes to city/state/region metadata. Admin-updatable. |
| **Commercial zone map** | A versioned mapping from (origin PIN, destination PIN) to Zone A–E for one Service or contract. Distinct from the Postal zone master (**A1-05**). |
| **Zone** | One of `A` (intra-city), `B` (intra-state/region), `C` (metro↔metro), `D` (rest of India), `E` (NE / J&K / special). **Not** to be confused with a Saved zone. |
| **Saved zone** | A named set of destination pincodes used by the `IN_SAVED_ZONE` rule operator. The brief's `zones` table maps here; it is renamed to avoid collision with Zone A–E, which is a pricing concept. **[rename]** |
| **Dead weight** | **F-24**. The physical weight of the parcel, in kg — the sum of its lines' per-unit weights × quantities, plus the package tare once. |
| **Volumetric weight** | **F-1**. Derived from package dimensions and the Service's divisor. |
| **Raw chargeable weight** | **F-2**. `max(dead, volumetric)`. Author term "chargeable weight" maps here. **[rename]** |
| **Billable weight** | **F-3**. Raw chargeable weight after the Service's minimum and rounding increment. **This is what money is computed on.** **[rename — the brief's single "chargeable weight" is split into these two]** |
| **Package profile** | A named box with L×W×H and a tare weight, selected per **F-20** (**A4-03**). Exactly one per Shop is the default (**INV-24**). |
| **Collectible** | The COD amount the courier must collect for a Shipment, in INR. Carried by exactly one Shipment per Order (**A3-01**, **INV-9**). |
| **COD unassigned** | The stored Order-level condition `order.cod_assignment_state = UNASSIGNED` (§3.24): the Order has COD outstanding but no Shipment with an active AWB carries it (**RV-03**, §4.7). |
| **Needs manual assignment** | The stored Shipment outcome `BOOKING_STATE = NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` (§3.2), with its cause in `shipment.manual_assignment_reason` (§3.30) and per-Service detail in the evaluation trace (**RV-03**). |
| **Unquoted Shipment** | A Shipment booked with no usable pre-booking price, recorded as `expected_cost_basis` = `PROVIDER_CONFIRMED_CHARGE` or `NONE` (§3.25) rather than `SNAPSHOT_QUOTE` (**RV-03**, **RV-04**). |
| **Rule** | A merchant-defined routing rule (§9.4). Evaluated top-down; first match wins. |
| **Carrier event status** | One of the 12 normalized values in `CARRIER_EVENT_STATUS` (§3.6) that every raw courier status maps to. **Replaces the brief's "13 standard statuses", which was the order-state list and is retired** (**A2-06**). **[rename]** |
| **NDR** | Non-delivery report — a delivery attempt that failed. |
| **RTO** | Return to origin — the parcel is returned to the pickup location. Courier-initiated only; customer-initiated returns do not exist in v1 (**RV-15**). |
| **Freight reconciliation** | Matching a courier's freight invoice to Jsyxi's expected cost, per `(AWB, charge type)` (**A2-05**). |
| **COD reconciliation** | Matching a courier's remittance to the Collectible of delivered COD Shipments (**A1-06**). |
| **Expected COD item** | A ledger row created when a Collectible-bearing Shipment is delivered; remittances allocate against it. |
| **AWB entitlement** | An append-only internal ledger of plan allowance debits and reversals. Separate from Shopify charge records (**A1-04**). |
| **Restricted** | The degraded account state entered on trial expiry, cancellation, payment failure or store freeze (**A2-08**, §3.11). |
| **Test shipment** | A Shipment booked on a Courier account in `TEST` mode. Exercises the full operational path; isolated from every figure, every Shopify write and every financial record (**A4-04**, **RV-08**, **INV-19**). |
| **Support context** | A time-limited, reason-bound, read-only admin session over one Shop (**A1-07**). |
| **Track token** | A random ≥128-bit, Shop-scoped, revocable token that opens one Shipment's public tracking page without further verification (**A1-07**, **A2-12**). |
| **Shop money** | The Shopify amount in the Shop's own currency (INR). All computation uses shop money (**A2-04**). |
| **Presentment money** | The buyer's checkout currency amount. Display only; never computed on (**A2-04**). |
| **Financial year** | Indian FY: 1 April – 31 March (**A1-11**). |
| **Occurred-at / Received-at** | The instant an external event happened vs. the instant Jsyxi received it. Both stored on every external event (**A1-10**). |

## 2. Canonical entities & primary keys

Every entity is Shop-scoped unless marked **[global]**. Every Shop-scoped table carries `shop_id` and every unique key, query, queue key, cache key, object path, export and signed URL includes it (**INV-1**).

Primary keys are opaque immutable internal IDs (UUID v4 unless stated). External identifiers are stored alongside, never used as PKs (**A1-10**).

Every **mutable** entity — `order`, `rule` and its children, `rate_card_version` while unsealed, `ticket`, `recon_freight_row`, `recon_cod_expected`, `shipment` while `DRAFT`, and every settings row — carries an integer `version` column incremented on each write, used for the optimistic concurrency check in **INV-22**.

**Enum completeness rule (RV-07).** Every column below whose name ends in `state`, `status`, `outcome`, `resolution`, `category`, `priority`, `kind`, `mode`, `basis`, `source`, `direction`, `scope` or `audience_kind` names its defining §3 subsection in the row. There are no value lists in §9 prose and none left to the implementer. **One exception, by name:** the `state` column on `pickup_location`, on `postal_pincode` and inside every recipient snapshot is the Indian **geographic** state — an address component, free text validated against the postal master, not a status enum.

### 2.9 The booking snapshot (**RV-05**)

**One instant, stated once here.** `shipment.snapshot` is assembled from the Shipment's working values and frozen at the **`DRAFT → QUEUED` transition** — the start of the first booking attempt — **after** rule evaluation and after any ship-modal override of Service or package profile. From that instant it is **immutable** (**INV-10**). Before it, the Shipment is a `DRAFT` whose working values are freely editable by an Operator+ (§10.4); rule evaluation, the ship-modal estimate and the persisted `rule_evaluation_trace` all read those same working values, so what the merchant saw is exactly what was frozen.

§3.2 and §10.4 cite this instant; neither restates it. A retry after `FAILED` or a rebook after a confirmed cancellation re-enters `DRAFT` and freezes a **new** snapshot on the next `DRAFT → QUEUED`, under a new booking intent (§9.5.4).

The snapshot contains, in full: recipient name / address lines / city / state / pincode / phone / email; allocation line IDs and quantities with SKU, title, variant, tags, unit price and HSN; `pickup_location` full address and GSTIN; `package_profile_id` with L×W×H and tare; payment mode and Collectible; dead weight (F-24) with its per-line derivation, volumetric weight, raw chargeable weight, billable weight; `service_id` + `service_version_id` with divisor, minimum and increment; `courier_account_id` and mode; `rate_card_version_id` and `zone_map_id` (null for `LIVE_QUOTE`); resolved origin/destination Zone; every formula input from §4; the full itemized expected quote with per-component amounts, currency, `cost_source`, `provider_quote_ref` and `fetched_at`; the Shopify order GID, line GIDs and fulfillment order GIDs; and `rule_id` + `rule_version` if the Service came from a rule.

---

## 3. Status enums & transition tables

Per **A1-02**, the brief's single 13-value "Order states" list is replaced by six independent machines (§3.1–§3.4, §3.10, §3.17) plus the supporting lifecycles and value lists in §3.11–§3.31. Every transition below names its actor, from-state, guard and reversibility, and **every terminal state is marked (terminal)**. A transition not listed does not exist; a state with no listed exit and no terminal marker is a defect to report.

**Completeness (RV-07).** Every status-like column on every entity in §2 has its complete value list here and is cited from its §2 row. Nothing in §9 introduces a value.

### 3.1 `ORDER_STATE` — import & eligibility (machine A)

`IMPORTED` · `INCOMPLETE` · `READY` · `PARTIALLY_BOOKED` · `FULLY_BOOKED` · `CLOSED` · `CANCELLED_IN_SHOPIFY`

| From | To | Actor | Guard | Reverse? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | `IMPORTED` | System (webhook/sweep) | Shopify order mirrored | n/a |
| `IMPORTED` | `INCOMPLETE` | System | Any booking hard-block in **INV-7** unmet | Yes → `READY` when fixed |
| `IMPORTED` / `INCOMPLETE` | `READY` | System | All **INV-7** conditions met and ≥1 unbooked allocation line | Yes → `INCOMPLETE` on a Shopify edit that breaks a condition |
| `READY` | `PARTIALLY_BOOKED` | System | ≥1 Shipment `CONFIRMED`, unbooked quantity remains | Yes (cancellation returns quantity) |
| `READY` / `PARTIALLY_BOOKED` | `FULLY_BOOKED` | System | All in-house allocation quantity carried by `CONFIRMED` Shipments | Yes (cancellation) |
| any | `CANCELLED_IN_SHOPIFY` **(terminal)** | System (`orders/cancelled`) | — | No |
| `FULLY_BOOKED` | `CLOSED` **(terminal)** | System | Every Shipment terminal (§3.4) and every COD expectation resolved | No |

An Order with zero Shipments displays its `ORDER_STATE`; an Order with Shipments displays the derived status in **F-22** (**A2-06**, pass-4 (c)).

### 3.2 `BOOKING_STATE` — booking outcome (machine B)

`DRAFT` · `NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` · `QUEUED` · `SUBMITTED` · `CONFIRMED` · `FAILED` · `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` · `VOID`

| From | To | Actor | Guard | Reverse? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | `DRAFT` | Member / System | Shipment created | n/a |
| `DRAFT` | `NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` | System | Routing produced no bookable Service, or payment mode is `UNRESOLVED` — cause stored in `manual_assignment_reason` (§3.30), per-Service detail in `rule_evaluation_trace` (**RV-03**) | Yes → `DRAFT` when a Member picks a Service manually or the cause is fixed |
| `DRAFT` | `QUEUED` | Member (`book`) / auto-ship | **INV-7** and **INV-9** satisfied; account not `RESTRICTED`; entitlement available or overage permitted. **The snapshot is frozen at this transition (§2.9)** | Yes → `DRAFT` if dequeued before submit |
| `QUEUED` | `SUBMITTED` | System worker | Booking intent created; digest computed | No |
| `SUBMITTED` | `CONFIRMED` | System | Provider returned an AWB; **INV-6** holds | No — reverse is cancellation (§3.3) |
| `SUBMITTED` | `FAILED` | System | Provider returned a definitive error | Yes → `DRAFT` via retry (new attempt, same Shipment, **new** booking intent and **new** snapshot) |
| `SUBMITTED` | `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | System | Transport timeout or ambiguous response | Only via reconciliation below |
| `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | `CONFIRMED` | System | Provider lookup by `merchant_reference` found the shipment | No |
| `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | `FAILED` | System / Operator+ | Provider lookup proved no shipment exists, **or** an Operator explicitly resolves it | Yes → `DRAFT` |
| `CONFIRMED` | `VOID` **(terminal)** | System | Courier-confirmed cancellation before any pickup event (§3.3) | No |

**A second create call MUST NOT be issued while a Shipment is `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`** (**INV-5**). No entitlement debit and no usage record may be created for an `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` Shipment.

`NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` is the single stored representation of the brief's "Needs manual assignment": F-22, the §9.10 dashboard action card, the §11 report row and every count read this value and this value only (**RV-03**).

### 3.3 `CUSTODY_STATE` — pickup & cancellation (machine C)

`NOT_APPLICABLE` · `PICKUP_PENDING` · `PICKUP_SCHEDULED` · `IN_CUSTODY` · `CANCEL_REQUESTED` · `CANCELLED` · `CANCEL_REJECTED`

| From | To | Actor | Guard | Reverse? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NOT_APPLICABLE` | `PICKUP_PENDING` | System | `BOOKING_STATE` = `CONFIRMED` | No |
| `PICKUP_PENDING` | `PICKUP_SCHEDULED` | Operator+ / System | `schedulePickup` acknowledged | Yes → `PICKUP_PENDING` if the courier cancels the pickup |
| `PICKUP_PENDING` / `PICKUP_SCHEDULED` | `IN_CUSTODY` **(terminal for this machine)** | System | First `PICKED_UP` carrier event | **No — this is the point of no return for cancellation.** Movement continues in machine D |
| `PICKUP_PENDING` / `PICKUP_SCHEDULED` | `CANCEL_REQUESTED` | Operator+ | `cancelShipment` submitted | Yes → previous state on rejection |
| `CANCEL_REQUESTED` | `CANCELLED` **(terminal)** | System | Courier confirmed cancellation | No |
| `CANCEL_REQUESTED` | `CANCEL_REJECTED` | System | Courier refused | Yes → `PICKUP_PENDING` |
| `CANCEL_REQUESTED` | `IN_CUSTODY` | System | A `PICKED_UP` event arrives while cancellation is pending — **the race in A1-04** | No. Flag for review; no entitlement reversal |

`NOT_APPLICABLE` is the state of every Shipment before `CONFIRMED`; it is not terminal and its only exit is the first row.

### 3.4 `MOVEMENT_STATE` — parcel movement, NDR and RTO (machine D)

`NOT_SHIPPED` · `IN_TRANSIT` · `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` · `NDR` · `DELIVERED` · `RTO_INITIATED` · `RTO_IN_TRANSIT` · `RTO_OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` · `RTO_DELIVERED` · `LOST_OR_DAMAGED` · `CANCELLED_BY_COURIER`

`NOT_SHIPPED` is the initial state and is left on the first carrier event. Driven **only** by normalized carrier events (§3.6) through this reducer:

| Carrier event | Sets `MOVEMENT_STATE` to |
|---|---|
| `PICKUP_SCHEDULED`, `PICKED_UP` | `IN_TRANSIT` |
| `IN_TRANSIT` | `IN_TRANSIT` |
| `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` | `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` |
| `UNDELIVERED_ATTEMPT` | `NDR` |
| `DELIVERED` | `DELIVERED` **(terminal)** |
| `RTO_INITIATED` | `RTO_INITIATED` |
| `RTO_IN_TRANSIT` | `RTO_IN_TRANSIT` |
| `RTO_OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` | `RTO_OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` |
| `RTO_DELIVERED` | `RTO_DELIVERED` **(terminal)** |
| `LOST_OR_DAMAGED` | `LOST_OR_DAMAGED` **(terminal)** |
| `CANCELLED_BY_COURIER` | `CANCELLED_BY_COURIER` **(terminal)** |

Reducer rules (**A1-10**): raw events are appended always; state is updated under an optimistic version check; **a terminal state is never silently regressed** — a later non-terminal event is stored, shown on the timeline, and raises a review flag instead of changing state; an event whose AWB resolves to no Shipment is quarantined for review, never dropped.

### 3.5 `PAYMENT_MODE`

`PREPAID` · `COD` · `UNRESOLVED`.

`COD` requires **both** conditions (**A1-03**): the Order's gateway name matches a COD entry in the merchant-maintained mapping (S-14), **and** F-15 order COD outstanding is greater than zero. A gateway that maps to COD but leaves nothing collectible — fully prepaid, fully captured or fully refunded — is `PREPAID`, not `COD`.

`PREPAID` is any Order whose gateways all map to prepaid entries and whose F-15 is zero.

`UNRESOLVED` covers both the unmapped gateway and the **mixed** case — an Order carrying both a mapped COD gateway and a mapped prepaid gateway, or a COD-mapped gateway whose collectible balance cannot be determined. `UNRESOLVED` blocks booking (**INV-7**) and puts the Shipment in `NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` with `manual_assignment_reason = PAYMENT_MODE_UNRESOLVED` (§3.2, §3.30), where a Member either corrects S-14 or sets the mode explicitly on that Order.

### 3.6 `CARRIER_EVENT_STATUS` — the only mapping target (**A2-06**)

`PICKUP_SCHEDULED` · `PICKED_UP` · `IN_TRANSIT` · `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` · `DELIVERED` · `UNDELIVERED_ATTEMPT` · `RTO_INITIATED` · `RTO_IN_TRANSIT` · `RTO_OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` · `RTO_DELIVERED` · `LOST_OR_DAMAGED` · `CANCELLED_BY_COURIER`

A raw courier status with no row in `courier_status_map` is stored on the raw timeline, **does not change any state**, and raises an admin alert in the Courier API error monitor (§9.13). The brief's phrase "the 13 standard statuses" is retired; it referred to the order-state list.

### 3.7 `COST_SOURCE` (**A2-02**)

`RATE_CARD` — priced from a Rate card version. `LIVE_QUOTE` — priced by the adapter's quote call. `NONE` — unpriceable: excluded from `CHEAPEST`, shows "no estimate", reconciles on weight only.

### 3.8 `RULE_ACTION_TYPE`

`PRIORITY_CHAIN` · `CHEAPEST` · `FASTEST`.

### 3.9 `RULE_CONDITION_FIELD` × `OPERATOR`

| Field | Operators | Operand semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `WEIGHT` | `EQUALS`, `BETWEEN`, `GTE`, `LTE` | **F-24 dead weight of the parcel**, not billable weight (**A1-03**). Ranges inclusive |
| `ORDER_AMOUNT` | `EQUALS`, `BETWEEN`, `GTE`, `LTE` | **F-17**, shop money. Ranges inclusive |
| `PAYMENT_MODE` | `IS_COD`, `IS_PREPAID` | §3.5 |
| `PINCODE` | `IN_LIST`, `NOT_IN_LIST`, `IN_SAVED_ZONE`, `CSV_UPLOAD` | **Destination** pincode |
| `SKU` / `TAG` | `IN_LIST`, `NOT_IN_LIST` | `IN_LIST` = **any** line on the Shipment matches; `NOT_IN_LIST` = **no** line matches (**A1-03**) |

Missing data for a condition evaluates to **no match** and is shown in the trace.

### 3.10 NDR (machine F)

`NDR_REASON`: `CUSTOMER_REFUSED` · `UNCONTACTABLE` · `ADDRESS_ISSUE` · `COD_NOT_READY` · `OTHER` — the fifth value exists so an unmappable courier reason is never discarded (**RV-14**, **INV-20**).

`NDR_ACTION`: `REATTEMPT` · `UPDATE_ADDRESS_AND_REATTEMPT` · `INITIATE_RTO`.

`NDR_CASE_STATE`: `OPEN` · `ACTION_SUBMITTED` · `REATTEMPT_SCHEDULED` · `RTO_REQUESTED` · `CLOSED`

| From | To | Actor | Guard | Reverse? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | `OPEN` | System | First `UNDELIVERED_ATTEMPT` carrier event for a Shipment with no open case | n/a |
| `OPEN` | `ACTION_SUBMITTED` | Operator+ / System (auto-reattempt, S-43) | An `ndr_action` was accepted by the adapter | Yes → `OPEN` if the provider rejects the action |
| `ACTION_SUBMITTED` | `REATTEMPT_SCHEDULED` | System | Provider acknowledged a reattempt | Yes → `OPEN` on a further `UNDELIVERED_ATTEMPT` (`attempt_count` increments) |
| `ACTION_SUBMITTED` | `RTO_REQUESTED` | System | Provider acknowledged an RTO initiation | No |
| `OPEN` / `ACTION_SUBMITTED` / `REATTEMPT_SCHEDULED` / `RTO_REQUESTED` | `CLOSED` **(terminal)** | System | The Shipment reached a terminal `MOVEMENT_STATE` (§3.4) | No — a later NDR on the same Shipment is impossible after a terminal state (**INV-17**) |

Aging is measured from `first_ndr_at`; the auto-RTO warning fires at S-44 while the case is not `CLOSED`.

### 3.11 `ACCOUNT_STATE` / `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE` (**A2-08**)

`TRIALING` · `ACTIVE` · `RESTRICTED` · `READ_ONLY` · `UNINSTALLED`

| From | To | Trigger | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRIALING`/`ACTIVE` | `RESTRICTED` | Trial expiry, cancellation, payment failure, store freeze | Blocks new booking, bulk booking, auto-ship and **new** label generation. Tracking ingestion, Shopify sync-back, NDR actions, reconciliation, tickets, reports, exports and re-download of existing documents all continue (pass-3 (c)) |
| `RESTRICTED` | `READ_ONLY` | S-40 elapsed (default 30 days) | Writes stop; retention continues per §5.4 |
| `RESTRICTED`/`READ_ONLY` | `ACTIVE` | Resubscribe | Full capability; new allowance period |
| any | `UNINSTALLED` **(terminal)** | Shopify uninstall | §9.1.5. Courier credentials destroyed. **No other state destroys a credential** |

### 3.12 `INVOICE_STATE` (**A2-07**)

`ISSUE_PENDING` · `ISSUED` · `VOID` **(terminal)**. The number is allocated **only** on `ISSUED`, so incomplete data produces no sequence gap; gaps arise only from `VOID`. Corrections are new linked void/credit/debit-note records, never edits (**A1-08**). `ISSUED` is terminal except for the single `ISSUED → VOID` transition, performed by Finance+ with a reason, audited.

### 3.13 `CHARGE_TYPE` (**A2-05**)

`FORWARD` · `RTO` · `REATTEMPT` · `COD_FEE` · `ADJUSTMENT` · `OTHER`. Default when a courier's invoice has no charge-type column: `FORWARD`. The expected-amount rule for **every** value is in §4.8 and is exhaustive by construction.

### 3.14 `RECON_WORKFLOW_STATE` (**A1-06**)

`OPEN` · `ACCEPTED` **(terminal)** · `DISPUTE_PREPARED` · `SUBMITTED` · `RESOLVED` **(terminal)** · `IGNORED` **(terminal)**. **Only `OPEN`, `DISPUTE_PREPARED` and `SUBMITTED` count as open disputes** on the dashboard and in reports. Mismatch flags (§2.7) are stored independently of this state and never overwritten by it.

### 3.15 `COD_EXPECTED_STATE`

`AWAITING` · `TALLIED` · `SHORT` · `EXCESS` · `PENDING_OVERDUE` · `RTO_UNCOLLECTED` **(terminal)**. Derived from cumulative allocations against tolerance (**F-13**) and the due date (**F-21**); every other value is recomputed whenever an allocation lands, so none is terminal.

### 3.16 Tickets

`TICKET_STATE`: `OPEN` · `IN_PROGRESS` · `RESOLVED` · `CLOSED` **(terminal)**. Reopening a `RESOLVED` ticket returns it to `IN_PROGRESS`; `CLOSED` requires a new ticket.

`TICKET_CATEGORY`: `COURIER_ISSUE` · `BILLING` · `BUG` · `FEATURE` · `OTHER` — the brief's five categories, defined here and not in §9 (**RW-17**).

`TICKET_PRIORITY`: `LOW` · `NORMAL` · `HIGH` · `URGENT`. Default `NORMAL` (**RW-17**).

### 3.17 `SYNC_STATE` — Shopify outbox (machine E)

`PENDING` · `IN_FLIGHT` · `SUCCEEDED` **(terminal)** · `RETRYING` · `DEAD`. Retries follow the single retry policy in **§8.6** (per S-48) and then move to a Shop-scoped DLQ with an alert. `DEAD` is exited only by an authorized admin replay, which returns the item to `PENDING`; every replay is audited (**A1-10**).

### 3.18 `RECON_BATCH_STATE`

`UPLOADED` · `PARSED` · `MATCHED` · `RESOLVED` **(terminal)** · `FAILED` **(terminal)**. Applies to both `recon_freight_batch` and `recon_cod_batch`. A batch reaches `RESOLVED` only when every row has a terminal `RECON_WORKFLOW_STATE` (§3.14) **and**, for freight batches, `control_total_state` (§3.28) is not `MISMATCH`. `FAILED` means the file could not be parsed or mapped; it holds no rows and is not idempotency-blocking, so a corrected file with the same content hash may be re-uploaded.

### 3.19 `ACCESS_REQUEST_RESOLUTION`

`PENDING` · `GRANTED` **(terminal)** · `DENIED` **(terminal)** · `WITHDRAWN` **(terminal)**. `PENDING` until an Owner acts or the requester withdraws; `GRANTED` implies a `shop_member` row was created in the same transaction (**RW-17**).

### 3.20 `USAGE_RECORD_STATE`

`PENDING` · `SUBMITTED` · `ACCEPTED` **(terminal)** · `REJECTED` **(terminal)** · `REVERSED` **(terminal)**. `REVERSED` is reached only where the verified Shopify API supports a safe reversal; otherwise a reversal is held as an `overage_credit` and the record stays `ACCEPTED` (§9.5.6, **RW-17**).

### 3.21 `COURIER_ACCOUNT_HEALTH`

`UNVERIFIED` · `HEALTHY` · `DEGRADED` · `DISCONNECTED` · `DISABLED`. `UNVERIFIED` until the first successful test-connection call; `DEGRADED` on repeated non-auth errors or an open circuit breaker; `DISCONNECTED` on an authentication or token-refresh failure — the trigger for the courier-disconnected alert (§9.21); `DISABLED` when the merchant switches the account off. None is terminal (**RW-17**).

### 3.22 `ALLOCATION_STATE`

`OPEN` · `PARTIALLY_BOOKED` · `FULLY_BOOKED` · `EXCLUDED` · `CLOSED` **(terminal)**. `EXCLUDED` is the state of an Allocation derived from fulfillment orders that are externally fulfilled or sit on a `ships_via_jsyxi = false` location — it is shown on the Order with its reason, never hidden (§9.2.3, **INV-20**, **RW-17**).

### 3.23 `BOOKING_INTENT_OUTCOME`

`IN_FLIGHT` · `CONFIRMED` **(terminal)** · `FAILED` **(terminal)** · `UNKNOWN` · `RESOLVED_CONFIRMED` **(terminal)** · `RESOLVED_FAILED` **(terminal)**. `UNKNOWN` is the intent-level counterpart of `BOOKING_STATE = OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`; the two `RESOLVED_*` values record that a `lookupByReference` call or an explicit Operator resolution closed it, and which way (§9.5.4, **RW-17**).

### 3.24 `COD_ASSIGNMENT_STATE` (**RV-03**)

`NOT_APPLICABLE` · `ASSIGNED` · `UNASSIGNED`. Stored on `order`. `NOT_APPLICABLE` when F-15 is zero. `ASSIGNED` while exactly one Shipment with an active AWB carries the full Collectible. `UNASSIGNED` is the stored form of "COD unassigned": F-15 is positive and no Shipment with an active AWB carries it, while at least one Shipment on the Order is already booked (§4.7). It is what the §9.10 dashboard card, the `COD_UNASSIGNED` report and the §9.21 notification all read (**RW-18**).

### 3.25 `EXPECTED_COST_BASIS` (**RV-03**, **RV-04**)

Stored on `shipment`; records where its reconciliation expectation comes from.

`SNAPSHOT_QUOTE` — a usable quote was frozen in the snapshot; §4.8 compares against F-23.
`PROVIDER_CONFIRMED_CHARGE` — no pre-booking quote, but the create response returned a confirmed charge, which becomes the expectation.
`NONE` — no pre-booking quote and no confirmed charge: the Shipment reconciles on **weight only** and its amount falls into the F-14 control-total residual (pass-4 (c)).

`PROVIDER_CONFIRMED_CHARGE` and `NONE` are together what the product calls an **unquoted** Shipment; they are filterable and shown on the shipment detail (**RW-18**).

### 3.26 `WEBHOOK_INBOX_STATE`

`RECEIVED` · `PROCESSING` · `PROCESSED` **(terminal)** · `FAILED` · `DEAD` **(terminal until an audited admin replay returns it to `RECEIVED`)**. `RECEIVED` is written durably **before** the 2xx acknowledgement (§8.1, §8.5); `FAILED` retries per S-48 (**RW-17**).

### 3.27 `JOB_STATE` — `document_job` and `report_job`

`QUEUED` · `RUNNING` · `SUCCEEDED` **(terminal)** · `PARTIAL` **(terminal)** · `FAILED` **(terminal)** · `CANCELLED` **(terminal)**. `PARTIAL` is the bulk-document case where some Shipments were skipped: the job still produces a document and a skipped report (§9.9.1, **RW-17**).

### 3.28 `CONTROL_TOTAL_STATE` (**RV-03**, **A3-05**)

Stored on `recon_freight_batch`. `WITHIN_THRESHOLD` · `MISMATCH` · `ACCEPTED_WITH_REMARK` **(terminal)**. `MISMATCH` is the stored form of the brief's `CONTROL_TOTAL_MISMATCH` and is what the dashboard disputes card counts as one item; `ACCEPTED_WITH_REMARK` requires a non-empty `residual_remark` and is audited (§4.8, §9.17.2, **RW-18**).

### 3.29 `ANNOUNCEMENT_AUDIENCE`

`ALL` · `BY_PLAN` · `SPECIFIC_SHOPS`. `audience_ref` holds the plan code or the Shop ID list and MUST be null for `ALL` (**RW-17**).

### 3.30 `MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT_REASON` (**RV-03**)

Non-null exactly when `BOOKING_STATE = NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT`.

`CHAIN_EXHAUSTED` — every Service in the matched chain failed serviceability or booking.
`NO_SERVICEABLE_CANDIDATE` — a `CHEAPEST` or `FASTEST` action found no serviceable Service at all.
`NO_RULE_AND_NO_DEFAULT_CHAIN` — no rule matched and S-22 is unset or its Services are all unusable.
`PAYMENT_MODE_UNRESOLVED` — §3.5.

The per-Service failure reasons behind any of these live in `rule_evaluation_trace.candidate_results` (§2.4) and are shown on the shipment and in the simulator (**RW-18**).

Declared inline in §2; listed here so §2 carries no value list of its own.

## 4. Computed fields & numeric policy

Every formula in the system is defined here, once. §9 references F-tags and never restates arithmetic.

### 4.1 Currency, precision & scale (**A1-05**, **A2-04**)

| Class | Storage | Display / settlement | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Money amount | `DECIMAL(19,4)` | INR to paise (2 dp) | ISO currency code stored on **every** financial row |
| Rate / ratio / percentage (stored) | `DECIMAL(12,6)` — 6 decimal places | as configured | Percent **inputs** are `0–100`; **stored** as `0–1` |
| Weight | `DECIMAL(10,3)` kg — 3 decimal places | per store weight unit (S-5) | kg is canonical; g is display/input only |
| Dimension | `DECIMAL(10,2)` cm — 2 decimal places | per store measurement unit (S-6) | cm is canonical; inch is display/input only |
| Count | integer | integer | — |

**Currency scope.** v1 ships domestic India only. A Shop's `shop_currency` MUST be `INR` (**INV-2**); onboarding blocks otherwise. **Presentment currency never blocks an order** — every computation uses shop money; presentment amount and currency are stored on the Order and shown only on the order detail screen, clearly labelled as the buyer's checkout currency (**A2-04**). There is no FX conversion anywhere in v1.

**Negative values.** Entered money, weight and dimensions MUST be positive. Only explicit adjustment, credit-note and entitlement-reversal rows may be signed.

**Rounding.** Round **half-up**, **per component**, **to paise**, at the moment the component is computed. The AWB total is the **sum of the stored rounded components** — never a re-round of an unrounded total (**INV-15**). There is no remainder-allocation problem in v1 because no rounded total is split back across lines; if a future feature splits one, this section is where the rule must be added.

**Zero/null guards.** A null divisor, null slab, null rate card version or null zone makes a Service unpriceable for that Shipment: it behaves as `COST_SOURCE = NONE` for that quote (excluded from `CHEAPEST`, "no estimate" shown), never as a zero price.

### 4.2 Weight

**F-24 · Dead weight of the parcel** (kg), per **RV-02**. Two levels — a **per-unit** ladder applied line by line, and **parcel-level** terms applied once:

1. **Per line**, resolve a **per-unit** weight, first hit wins:
   `sku_override.weight_kg` for that line's SKU → `order_line.weight_kg_override` → the Shopify line weight per unit.
   A line where none of the three yields a value resolves to **0.000 kg** and is listed as "no weight" on the ship modal and in the bulk skipped report, so the merchant can fix it (**INV-20**).
2. **Multiply** each line's per-unit weight by `shipment_line.quantity` and **sum across the Shipment's lines** → `line_weight_total`.
3. If `line_weight_total = 0` — no line on the parcel yielded any weight — substitute the store default **parcel** weight **S-7**, applied **once**. S-7 is a per-parcel fallback and is never added per line.
4. **Add the resolved package profile's `tare_kg` once for the parcel** (F-20 selects the profile).

`F-24 = (line_weight_total > 0 ? line_weight_total : S-7) + package_profile.tare_kg`

`package_profile.tare_kg` and S-7 are parcel-level quantities and MUST NOT appear in the per-line chain in step 1. **INV-7** requires F-24 to be positive before booking.

**F-1 · Volumetric weight** (kg) = `(length_cm × width_cm × height_cm) ÷ service_version.volumetric_divisor`, to 3 dp. Dimensions come from the F-20 package profile.

**F-2 · Raw chargeable weight** (kg) = `max(F-24, F-1)`.

**F-3 · Billable weight** (kg) = `max(service_version.min_billable_kg, ceil(F-2 ÷ service_version.billable_increment_kg) × service_version.billable_increment_kg)`. Default increment 0.5 kg.

> **Worked example A — single line, single unit.** One line, quantity 1, Shopify line weight 0.380 kg/unit, no SKU or line override. Package profile "Small box" 25 × 20 × 10 cm, tare 0.040 kg. Service divisor 5000, minimum 0.5 kg, increment 0.5 kg.
> F-24 = (1 × 0.380) + 0.040 = **0.420 kg**.
> F-1 = (25 × 20 × 10) ÷ 5000 = 5000 ÷ 5000 = **1.000 kg**. F-2 = max(0.420, 1.000) = **1.000 kg**. F-3 = max(0.5, ceil(1.000 ÷ 0.5) × 0.5) = max(0.5, 2 × 0.5) = **1.000 kg**.

> **Worked example B — multi-line, multi-quantity (RV-02).** Three lines on one parcel. Line 1 `TSHIRT-M`, quantity **3**, SKU override 0.250 kg/unit. Line 2 `MUG-01`, quantity **2**, no override, Shopify line weight 0.400 kg/unit. Line 3 `STICKER`, quantity 1, no weight anywhere. Package profile "Medium box" 30 × 24 × 12 cm, tare 0.080 kg. Service divisor 5000, minimum 0.5 kg, increment 0.5 kg.
> Per line: 3 × 0.250 = 0.750 · 2 × 0.400 = 0.800 · 1 × 0.000 = 0.000 *(flagged "no weight")*. `line_weight_total` = **1.550 kg**.
> `line_weight_total > 0`, so S-7 is **not** used. F-24 = 1.550 + 0.080 (tare, once) = **1.630 kg**.
> F-1 = (30 × 24 × 12) ÷ 5000 = 8640 ÷ 5000 = **1.728 kg**. F-2 = max(1.630, 1.728) = **1.728 kg**. F-3 = max(0.5, ceil(1.728 ÷ 0.5) × 0.5) = max(0.5, 4 × 0.5) = **2.000 kg**.
> The two errors this example exists to prevent: weighing line 1 as 0.250 kg (ignoring quantity 3) and adding the 0.080 kg tare three times (once per line).

### 4.3 Zone

**F-4 · Zone resolution.** Given the Shipment's origin pincode (the pickup location) and destination pincode: evaluate the `commercial_zone_rule` rows of the Rate card version's referenced `zone_map_id` in `position` order; first match wins; the matched row's `zone` (A–E) is the result. Zone rules resolve pincode attributes (city, district, state, region, metro, special) from the **`postal_version_id` frozen on that zone map**, never from the current postal master (**A1-05**). No match → the Service is unpriceable for that lane (§4.1 zero/null guard).

`LIVE_QUOTE` Services have no zone map; F-4 is not evaluated for them.

### 4.4 Freight components (`RATE_CARD` Services)

Let `W` = F-3 billable weight and `S` = the matched `rate_card_slab` for the resolved Zone.

**F-5 · Base freight** = `S.base_rate + (additional_steps × S.additional_rate)` where
`additional_steps = 0` if `W ≤ S.base_weight_kg`, else `ceil((W − S.base_weight_kg) ÷ S.additional_step_kg)`.

**F-6 · Fuel surcharge** = `rate_card_version.fuel_pct × F-5`. Basis is forward freight (**A1-05**).

**F-7 · COD charge** = `0` when `PAYMENT_MODE ≠ COD` or the Shipment carries no Collectible; else `max(rate_card_version.cod_flat, rate_card_version.cod_pct × shipment.collectible)`. Basis is the **Collectible**, not the order amount (**A1-05**).

**F-8 · Other surcharges** = `Σ` over the version's `rate_card_component` rows (§2.3) in `position` order, each computed on its own `basis`: `FLAT` → `value`; `PERCENT_OF_BASE_FREIGHT` → `value × F-5`; `PERCENT_OF_PRE_TAX_SUBTOTAL` → `value × (F-5 + F-6 + F-7)`; `PER_KG_BILLABLE` → `value × F-3`. **A version with no component rows makes F-8 = ₹0.00**, which is the seeded default (**RW-19**). Each component is rounded and stored individually per **INV-15**, and its `is_taxable` flag feeds F-10.

**F-9 · Pre-tax subtotal** = `F-5 + F-6 + F-7 + F-8`.

**F-10 · GST** = `rate_card_version.gst_pct × (sum of the components marked taxable in rate_card_version.taxable_components, plus every rate_card_component row with is_taxable = true)`. **Default: every component is taxable**, so by default F-10 = `gst_pct × F-9`, with `gst_pct` defaulting to 18% (**A2-10**). GST is a versioned per-contract value, never a hard-coded constant (**A1-05**).

**F-11 · Total expected freight** = `F-9 + F-10`, computed as the sum of the stored rounded components (**INV-15**).

**Component order** is `F-5 → F-6 → F-7 → F-8 → F-9 → F-10 → F-11` (**A2-10**). F-7 is computed on the Collectible independently of F-6 — fuel does not enter the COD basis. The order and the taxable set are stored on the Rate card version and are versioned per contract.

**F-12 · RTO charge** = computed at RTO initiation from the **booking snapshot**. For a `RATE_CARD` Service, use the snapshot's Rate card version `rto_basis`: `SAME_AS_FORWARD` → the snapshot's F-5, or `PERCENT_OF_FORWARD` → `rto_pct × snapshot F-5`. For a `LIVE_QUOTE` Service, use the `rto_rule` returned on the snapshotted quote (§8.3) and interpret it identically; when the provider returned no `rto_rule`, **there is no RTO expectation** — an invoice row with `charge_type = RTO` for that AWB sets `flag_review` rather than a false amount mismatch, exactly as §4.8 handles an unquoted Shipment. Fuel, other surcharges and GST apply to the RTO charge on the same terms as forward (**A2-10**).

> **Worked example (continues example A).** Ahmedabad 380015 → New Delhi 110001, resolved Zone C, COD order of ₹2,000, F-3 = 1.000 kg. Slab: first 0.5 kg = ₹42.00, each additional 0.5 kg = ₹38.00. Fuel 18%. COD: flat ₹35.00 or 2%, whichever is greater. No `rate_card_component` rows. GST 18%, all components taxable.
> F-5 = 42.00 + (ceil((1.000 − 0.5) ÷ 0.5) = 1) × 38.00 = **₹80.00**
> F-6 = 0.18 × 80.00 = **₹14.40**
> F-7 = max(35.00, 0.02 × 2000.00 = 40.00) = **₹40.00**
> F-8 = **₹0.00** (no component rows)
> F-9 = 80.00 + 14.40 + 40.00 + 0.00 = **₹134.40**
> F-10 = 0.18 × 134.40 = 24.192 → half-up to paise = **₹24.19**
> F-11 = 134.40 + 24.19 = **₹158.59**

### 4.5 Quote, cost source & candidate elimination (**A2-02**, **A3-04**, **RV-04**)

`RATE_CARD` Services produce a quote from F-5…F-11. `LIVE_QUOTE` Services produce a quote from the adapter's `getQuote` response (§8.3), which MUST return the same itemized shape. `NONE` Services produce no quote and show "no estimate".

**Quote freshness.** A `LIVE_QUOTE` is cached on `(service_id, origin_pincode, destination_pincode, billable_weight_band, payment_mode)` with TTL S-16 (default 15 minutes). At booking, a quote older than its TTL is re-fetched.

**Quote budget.** Quote calls carry a per-courier-account budget (S-17) alongside the booking rate limiter, at **lower priority than booking calls** — quoting MUST NOT starve booking on the same courier (**A3-04**). Within a bulk job, distinct cache keys are pre-resolved once before the booking stage and reused across orders; each distinct key is fetched at most once per job.

**Candidate elimination — one rule per action, never merged** (**RV-04**). These three bullets are the only place elimination is defined; §4.9, §9.4.3 and §9.4.4 cite them.

- **`CHEAPEST`.** A Service with no usable price — quote failure, exhausted budget, `COST_SOURCE = NONE`, or a §4.1 zero/null guard — **is excluded**, with the structured reason in the trace. A missing or stale EDD does **not** exclude a Service from `CHEAPEST`. If **no** candidate has a usable price, fall back to the merchant's priority chain and record "price unavailable — fell back to chain" (**A2-12**); if the chain is also exhausted, `NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` with `NO_SERVICEABLE_CANDIDATE`.
- **`FASTEST`.** A Service with a missing or stale EDD (**F-18**) **is excluded**, with the reason in the trace. A missing or failed **price** alone never excludes a Service from `FASTEST` — price is not this action's deciding input. If **no** candidate has a usable EDD, fall back to the merchant's priority chain and record why (**A1-03**); if the chain is also exhausted, `NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` with `NO_SERVICEABLE_CANDIDATE`.
- **`PRIORITY_CHAIN`.** **Neither a missing price nor a missing EDD ever excludes a Service** (**A3-04**). The chain position books at the Service the merchant chose, in order, and only a serviceability failure or a booking failure moves down the chain. If every position fails, `NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT` with `CHAIN_EXHAUSTED`.

**Recording an unquoted booking.** Every Shipment stores an `expected_cost_basis` (§3.25) at snapshot time: `SNAPSHOT_QUOTE` when a usable quote was frozen; `PROVIDER_CONFIRMED_CHARGE` when there was none but the create response returned a confirmed charge, which becomes the expectation; `NONE` when there was neither — that AWB reconciles on **weight only** and its amount falls into the F-14 control-total residual (pass-4 category (c)). `expected_amount` is null exactly when the basis is `NONE`.

### 4.6 Order money

**F-17 · Order amount** — the `ORDER_AMOUNT` rule operand and the reports figure — = the Shopify current total payable in **shop money** after discounts, tax, shipping and refunds (**A1-03**, **A2-04**).

**F-15 · Order COD outstanding** = `F-17 − amounts already captured or paid − refunds`, floored at 0, in shop money. For a fully prepaid order this is 0. This is the quantity **INV-9** balances.

### 4.7 Collectible allocation (**A3-01**, **A4-01**, **RV-06**, **RV-11**)

The Collectible is an attribute of the **Shipment**. Exactly one Shipment per **Order** carries the full F-15 outstanding balance; every other Shipment on that Order books with `collectible = 0` as a prepaid docket and is priced with F-7 = 0.

**When an Order has more than one Shipment.** Only via the §9.2.3 fallback path — one Shipment per unmergeable Shopify fulfillment order. There is no merchant-initiated parcel split in v1 (**RV-06**), so the rules below are reached exactly when Shopify itself split the order and merging was unavailable. They are **not** dead code (**INV-9**).

- Default carrier: the **first Shipment booked on the Order**. A Member may move it to another not-yet-booked Shipment on the same Order from the ship modal before booking; it cannot be moved once any sibling is booked.
- **INV-9** is enforced inside the booking transaction, keyed on the **Order** — a row-level lock or a unique partial index on `(order_id) WHERE collectible > 0` — so parallel bulk booking of sibling Shipments cannot both claim it.
- On confirmed cancellation of the Collectible-bearing Shipment, the Collectible returns to the Order and is claimed by the next Shipment booked on it. If every remaining Shipment is already booked, `order.cod_assignment_state` becomes `UNASSIGNED` (§3.24) — surfaced as a dashboard action card, a report row and a notification; the Member either cancels and rebooks one Shipment to carry it, or accepts the Order as uncollected. It is **never** silently dropped.
- If the Collectible-bearing Shipment goes RTO while a sibling delivers, record `RTO_UNCOLLECTED` (§3.15) — **never** a Short remittance.
- Proportional splitting of a Collectible across parcels is **not done in v1**.

> **Worked example.** Order 1042, COD, F-15 = ₹2,000.00. Shopify split it across two locations and the API refused the merge, so §9.2.3's fallback produced Shipment A (booked 10:14) and Shipment B (booked 10:15). A.collectible = ₹2,000.00 and pays F-7; B.collectible = ₹0.00 and F-7 = ₹0.00. Sum = ₹2,000.00 = F-15 ✓ and `cod_assignment_state = ASSIGNED`. A is later cancelled before pickup while B is already booked → `cod_assignment_state = UNASSIGNED`.

### 4.8 Reconciliation arithmetic

**F-23 · Audited freight quote** = F-5…F-11 recomputed with the **invoiced** billable weight substituted for F-3, using the immutable tariff, zone map and divisor from the booking snapshot. This is what an invoice amount is compared against, so a legitimate reweigh charge is flagged as a weight difference and **not** double-flagged as an amount difference (**A1-06**).

**Tolerances resolve per courier account, then per Shop** (**A1-06**): the effective tolerance is `courier_account.<tolerance>` when set, else the Shop default in §7.5. Every comparison below uses the effective value.

**Freight flags** are independent booleans evaluated per `(AWB, charge_type)` row (**A2-05**):
- `flag_awb_not_found` — the AWB matches no Shipment in this Shop.
- `flag_weight_mismatch` — `abs(invoiced_weight − snapshot billable weight) > effective weight tolerance` (default 0.01 kg).
- `flag_amount_mismatch` — `abs(invoiced_amount − expected_for_charge_type) > effective freight tolerance` (default ₹1.00).

**`expected_for_charge_type` — exhaustive over `CHARGE_TYPE` (§3.13) by construction.** Every value has a row; there is no fall-through:

| `charge_type` | Expected amount | If it cannot be computed |
|---|---|---|
| `FORWARD` | **F-23** | `expected_cost_basis = PROVIDER_CONFIRMED_CHARGE` → the confirmed charge; `NONE` → no expectation, `flag_review` |
| `RTO` | **F-12** recomputed on the invoiced weight | No `rto_rule` on the snapshot → no expectation, `flag_review` (§4.4) |
| `COD_FEE` | The snapshot's **F-7** | Snapshot has no F-7 (unquoted) → no expectation, `flag_review` |
| `REATTEMPT` | **No expectation** — `flag_review`, never a false amount mismatch (**A2-05**) | — |
| `ADJUSTMENT` | The amount is compared against **the row it adjusts** (`adjusts_row_id`): the adjustment is added to that row's invoiced total and the sum re-compared against that row's expectation (**RW-24**) | No linked row identifiable → no expectation, `flag_review`. An `ADJUSTMENT` is always an append-only linked record and never overwrites the row it adjusts (**A1-06**) |
| `OTHER` | **No expectation** — `flag_review` (**A2-05**) | — |

Multiple rows of the same charge type for one AWB are **summed before comparison**. A row whose charge type cannot be mapped from the courier's own value gets `flag_review` and appears in the disputes list; it is never silently dropped or auto-accepted (**INV-20**).

**F-14 · Control total residual** (**A3-05**) = `batch.declared_invoice_total − Σ(matched row amounts) − Σ(review row amounts)`.
`control_total_state` (§3.28) = `MISMATCH` when `abs(F-14) > max(₹100, 0.5% × declared_invoice_total)` (S-19 / S-20), else `WITHIN_THRESHOLD`; a Finance+ acceptance with a remark moves it to `ACCEPTED_WITH_REMARK`. A batch cannot reach `RESOLVED` while `control_total_state = MISMATCH` (§3.18).

> **Worked example (continues example A).** The courier invoices AWB `DL0087412391` at 1.500 kg, ₹211.50, `charge_type = FORWARD`. Booked billable weight was 1.000 kg.
> Weight: |1.500 − 1.000| = 0.500 > 0.01 → **`flag_weight_mismatch` = true**.
> F-23 at 1.500 kg: F-5 = 42.00 + (ceil((1.500 − 0.5) ÷ 0.5) = 2) × 38.00 = ₹118.00; F-6 = ₹21.24; F-7 = ₹40.00; F-8 = ₹0.00; F-9 = ₹179.24; F-10 = 0.18 × 179.24 = 32.2632 → ₹32.26; F-11 = **₹211.50**.
> Amount: |211.50 − 211.50| = 0.00 ≤ ₹1.00 → **`flag_amount_mismatch` = false**. The row is a pure weight dispute — exactly the outcome A1-06 requires.
>
> Batch level: declared invoice total ₹2,50,000.00; matched rows ₹2,47,300.00; review rows ₹1,200.00. F-14 = 250000 − 247300 − 1200 = **₹1,500.00**. Threshold = max(100, 0.005 × 250000 = 1250) = ₹1,250.00. 1500 > 1250 → **`control_total_state = MISMATCH`**.

**F-21 · COD due date** = `delivered_at + effective cod_due_days` (default 7 calendar days), where the effective value is the Shipment's `courier_account.cod_due_days` when set, else the Shop default S-30. Evaluated in shop-local time. An expectation with no full allocation after its due date becomes `PENDING_OVERDUE`; aging days = calendar days since `due_at`.

**F-13 · COD tally.** Let `R` = the sum of allocations against one expectation and `tolerance` = the effective COD tolerance. `TALLIED` if `abs(R − expected) ≤ tolerance`; `SHORT` if `R < expected − tolerance`; `EXCESS` if `R > expected + tolerance`; `AWAITING` while `R = 0` and now < `due_at`.

### 4.9 Identity, staleness & derived display

**F-19 · AWB normalization** = trim → strip all whitespace and hyphens → upper-case. Uniqueness and every comparison use the normalized value; the raw value is preserved (**A1-10**).

**F-18 · EDD staleness.** An EDD is stale when `now − quote.fetched_at > S-18` (default 6 hours). A Service with a missing or stale EDD is excluded from **`FASTEST` only**; §4.5 states the full per-action rule and this formula does not restate it (**RV-04**).

**F-20 · Package profile selection** (**A4-03**): a `sku_override.package_profile_id` matching any Shipment line's SKU → the first matching `package_selection_rule` in `position` order → the Shop's `is_default` package profile, which **INV-24** guarantees is exactly one. When two lines carry different SKU overrides, the profile with the largest volume wins (**RV-14**). The ship modal shows the resolved profile and allows a per-Shipment override; bulk booking and auto-ship use the resolved profile without prompting. The resolved profile ID, its L×W×H and its `tare_kg` enter the snapshot at `DRAFT → QUEUED` (§2.9), so later edits to the profile never change a booked Shipment's F-24 or F-1.

**F-22 · Derived order shipping status** (**A2-06**). For an Order with ≥1 Shipment, apply first-match precedence across its Shipments: `Manual assignment needed` (any Shipment with `BOOKING_STATE = NEEDS_MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT`, §3.2) → `NDR` → `RTO in progress` (any non-terminal RTO state) → `Booking failed` → any in-flight movement state (**least advanced wins**) → `Delivered` (only when every Shipment is `DELIVERED`) → `Cancelled` (only when all are cancelled). Mixed terminal outcomes render as `Partially delivered`. An Order with **zero** Shipments displays its `ORDER_STATE` (§3.1).

### 4.10 Performance metrics (**A1-11**)

**F-16.a Delivery rate** = `Delivered ÷ (Delivered + RTO Delivered)` over a **booked cohort**; open Shipments are shown separately and appear in neither term.
**F-16.b NDR rate** = `Shipments with ≥1 NDR ÷ Picked-up shipments`.
**F-16.c RTO rate** = `RTO Delivered ÷ Terminal shipments`.
**F-16.d TAT** = calendar hours from the `PICKED_UP` occurred-at to the `DELIVERED` occurred-at.

Every metric counts **Shipments** by default; any figure counted per Order is labelled as such on the card and in the export header (**A2-06**). Test shipments are excluded from all of them (**INV-19**).

---

## 5. Scale, temporal & data-lifecycle assumptions

### 5.1 Volume & growth (**A1-09**)

10,000 shipments/day and 150,000 normalized tracking events/day are **platform-wide steady-state launch load**, not per merchant. Size year one for ≥3.65 million Shipments and ≥55 million tracking events. `tracking_event` is the fastest-growing table; it and `tracking_event_raw` are partitioned by month, as is `shipment`.

**Test shipments are excluded from every figure in this section** (**INV-19**, **RV-08**): they do not count toward the daily envelope, the year-one sizing or the load-test targets. Capacity planning measures live shipments only.

Load-test targets: 3× short bursts; a two-hour provider-outage catch-up; 250 concurrent dashboard actors; 20 simultaneous 1,000-shipment bulk jobs. Configurable per-Shop concurrency and rate quotas (S-21) MUST prevent one merchant starving shared workers or provider limits.

Largest single things: bulk booking ≤1,000 orders per job; bulk label PDF ≤1,000 Shipments; freight/COD import ≤50 MB and ≤250,000 rows; rate-card/zone import ≤25 MB and ≤100,000 rows; ticket attachments 5 files × 10 MB; feedback 1 PNG/JPEG × 10 MB (**A1-12**). Provider-specific lower limits still apply.

### 5.2 Temporal policy (**A1-11**)

- **Storage:** all instants in UTC. Every external event stores both `occurred_at` and `received_at`.
- **Display & derivation:** business dates render and derive in the Shop's IANA timezone (default `Asia/Kolkata`). Local ranges are half-open `[00:00, next 00:00)`. Week starts **Monday**. Financial year is **1 April – 31 March**.
- **Date vs datetime:** `invoice_date`, `remittance_date`, `effective_from`, `effective_to` and `due_at` are **dates**; every other temporal field is a datetime.
- **Backdating:** system booking and tracking instants can never be backdated. Invoice and remittance dates may be historical but **never** future-dated. Upload and correction times are immutable separate instants.
- **Scheduled work** — reports, digests, auto-ship sweeps, NDR aging — runs in shop-local time.
- **Period attribution:** Orders → Shopify created-at. Shipments and cost → booked-at. NDR → first-NDR-at. RTO → RTO-initiated-at. Delivery and TAT → delivered occurred-at. Reconciliation → invoice/remittance date, with upload date separately filterable.
- **Freshness:** dashboards may lag ≤75 minutes and MUST display an as-of time. Exports are immutable snapshots as of job start; later corrections restate live dashboards but never rewrite an exported artifact.

### 5.3 Deletion semantics per entity (**A1-08**)

| Policy | Entities |
|---|---|
| **Hard delete** (only while unused) | Draft rules, unused saved zones, unused package profiles (never the `is_default` one — **INV-24**), unsent draft tickets |
| **Deactivate** (referenced, never deleted) | `courier`, `service`, `courier_account`, `merchant_service`, `pickup_location`, `rule`, `saved_zone`, `package_profile`, `label_template`, `import_column_map` |
| **Append-only / immutable** | `rate_card_version` once used, `shipment` and its snapshot **except `is_test = true` rows (see the carve-out below)**, `booking_intent`, `tracking_event*`, `gst_invoice` once issued, `awb_entitlement_ledger`, `usage_record`, every `recon_*` row, `audit_log` |

**Test-data carve-out (RV-08).** A Shipment with `is_test = true`, and every child record it owns — its `booking_intent` rows, `tracking_event` and `tracking_event_raw` rows, `ndr_case` and `ndr_action` rows, `document` rows and its `rule_evaluation_trace` — is **exempt from the append-only rule above** and may be bulk-deleted by the Owner at any time (§9.5.7, §10.2). The exemption is stated here rather than left to a retention note, and it is closed over the class: no child of a test Shipment is append-only. Test Shipments never produce an entitlement ledger entry, a usage record, a GST invoice or a reconciliation row, so none of those tables ever needs the exemption (**INV-19**).

References **block** deletion; they never cascade. Corrections to immutable facts use cancellation, reversal, adjustment or a new linked version — never an edit (**INV-16**).

### 5.4 Retention horizons (**A1-08**, **RV-12**)

**OWNER: Mahesh Rojasara.** These values are a **buildable instruction, not an open question**: Mahesh confirms or amends them before the hardening phase begins; if that review has not happened by the start of hardening, the values below are built exactly as written and the review becomes a post-launch change (**RV-12**).

| Data | Horizon |
|---|---|
| Financial, tax, billing, reconciliation, shipment and audit facts; invoice PDFs | 7 financial years |
| Normalized tracking events | 24 months |
| Raw webhook payloads | 30 days |
| Report exports | 30 days |
| Labels, manifests, temporary bundles | 90 days |
| Ticket and feedback attachments | 180 days after closure/submission |
| Test shipments and every child record in the §5.3 carve-out | the shortest applicable horizon above; the Owner may bulk-delete them at any time (**RV-08**) |

### 5.5 Offboarding & privacy (**A1-08**)

**Uninstall** immediately invalidates all sessions and public track tokens; disables webhooks, polling, schedules and queued jobs; and **destroys both the test and live courier credential sets** and the Shopify credentials. Reinstall is a fresh connection, never a restore. No other account state destroys a credential (**A2-08**).

**Privacy redaction** (`customers/redact`, `shop/redact`, `customers/data_request`) removes or irreversibly pseudonymizes PII from primary tables, search indexes, rollups, object storage, exports, caches and later-expiring backups, retaining only specifically justified non-PII financial facts. Deletion evidence is recorded. Redaction revokes buyer track access.

### 5.6 Day one (**A1-08**)

**Seed before the first login:** courier and service definitions with capabilities and versions; raw→carrier-event status maps; a postal zone master version; the fixed enums in §3; default plan tiers; a default label template; **exactly one default package profile per Shop** (**INV-24**); default import column maps per courier.

**Backfill:** the optional 30-day import brings in **open/unfulfilled Shopify orders only**. Legacy AWBs, in-flight tracking, historical invoices and remittances, and opening disputes are explicitly **out of scope** and would require a separate migration that v1 does not provide.

### 5.7 Platform constraints (author-locked)

**The BYOC money boundary is the first of these constraints and the one most easily re-derived away — see INV-23.** It is a commercial and regulatory position, not a design preference, and §9.15 (rate cards) and §9.17.3 (remittance matching) are the two screens where an implementer would most naturally violate it.

Node.js (NestJS) + TypeScript · PostgreSQL 15+ (partitioning per §5.1; read replica for dashboards and reports) · Redis + BullMQ · S3-compatible object storage · Docker with horizontally scaled workers.

**Queues:** `order-ingest` · `booking` (partitioned per Service, with a per-courier rate limiter and circuit breaker so one courier's outage never blocks another) · `label` · `tracking-ingest` · `shopify-sync` · `recon-processing` · `reports` · `notifications`.

**Architectural requirements that affect correctness:** dashboard and report figures come from maintained hourly rollup tables, never per-row subqueries at render time; webhook ingest is stateless and acknowledges within the budgets in §8.1 and §8.5; every queue has a DLQ with per-Service success metrics and a per-Shop sync-lag metric.

**Security controls (author-locked, `brief.txt` §3).** All six are requirements, not aspirations:

1. **Courier credentials are envelope-encrypted at rest.** A per-record data key encrypts each credential blob — test and live are two independent blobs (§2.2) — and that data key is itself encrypted by a KMS-managed master key. Master keys are rotatable without re-encrypting stored records. The ciphertext is decryptable only inside the relevant adapter worker at call time (**INV-18**).
2. **TLS 1.2 or higher on every external connection** — Shopify Admin API calls, courier API calls, inbound Shopify and courier webhooks (§8.1, §8.5), the dashboard and admin surfaces, the public track-order page (§9.16), and every signed document URL (S-26). Plaintext HTTP is refused, not redirected.
3. **Secrets masked in the UI.** Credential fields are write-only with a masked display and a "replace" action; no role, including Owner, can read one back (§10.2).
4. **No PII in logs.** Application, worker, transport and error logs MUST NOT contain buyer or merchant personal data — no recipient name, address, phone, email, or raw courier request/response bodies containing them. Logs carry internal IDs and masked summaries only. Where a value must be correlated (a phone in an abuse log, §9.16), store a salted hash, never the value.
5. **Full audit log** — §12.
6. **Signed Shopify-entry tokens** — §9.1.1.

**Shopify compliance (author-locked, `brief.txt` §3, field set settled by RV-13).** GraphQL Admin API only (§8.4) · HMAC on all webhooks (§8.1) · GDPR webhooks with real redaction jobs (§5.5) · all charges via the Shopify Billing API (§9.14) · **Protected Customer Data at Level 2**: the app requests Level 2 access; the protected fields collected are **recipient name, address lines, city, state, pincode, phone and email**; the declared purposes are **courier label and manifest generation** (§9.9.1), **booking payloads to courier adapters** (§8.2, §8.3), and the **Track-Order page lookup and timeline** (§9.16). The minimisation and retention commitments backing that justification are §2.9 (snapshot scope), §5.4 (retention), §5.5 (redaction), §7.6 S-36 and §9.16 (the page never exposes address, contact data, credentials or order totals), §10.3 (support context never exports PII) and §12 (no raw buyer PII in abuse logs). **The request is submitted before build week 1 — it has approval lead time and gates launch** (**RV-13**, §14 week 0).

## 6. Global invariants

Always true, and each is enforced in code, not by convention. Where an invariant has a legitimate transient exception, the exception is stated in the invariant itself rather than left to be discovered.

- **INV-1 · Tenancy.** `shop_id` scopes every merchant-owned row, unique key, query, queue key, cache key, object path, export and signed URL. No query may return another Shop's row. Sessions bind to **both** `shop_id` and the current Shopify staff-user identity; revoked access or uninstall invalidates sessions and stops new jobs (**A1-07**).
- **INV-2 · Currency.** `shop.shop_currency = 'INR'`, and every financial row stores its ISO currency code. No FX conversion exists in v1 (**A1-05**, **A2-04**).
- **INV-3 · Single pickup location.** Exactly one `pickup_location` row per Shop has `is_active = true` at v1 (**A3-01**, **A4-02**).
- **INV-4 · One shipment, one parcel.** A Shipment carries exactly one piece in v1. The quote contract keeps a `pieces` field fixed at 1 for forward compatibility (**A2-12**).
- **INV-5 · No second create under ambiguity.** While `BOOKING_STATE = OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, no further `createShipment` call, entitlement debit or usage record may be issued for that Shipment (**A1-04**).
- **INV-6 · AWB uniqueness.** Unique on `(shop_id, courier_account_id, awb_normalized)`. A Shipment has at most one active AWB (**A1-04**).
- **INV-7 · Booking hard-blocks.** Booking is blocked — not warned — when any of these is missing or invalid: recipient name, address, 6-digit Indian destination pincode, 10-digit phone; allocated lines with positive quantity; **positive F-24 parcel weight** and positive dimensions; pickup location; resolved payment mode and Collectible; an enabled, serviceable Service; valid courier credentials for the account's current `mode`. Order **sync** may retain incomplete orders; only booking blocks (**A1-02**). **GST-invoice data is deliberately NOT in this list** (**A2-07**). Every condition is evaluable from data that exists at the moment the block fires: all of them are working values on the `DRAFT` Shipment (§2.9), none is computed later.
- **INV-8 · Snapshot-based evaluation.** Costing, labels, documents and reconciliation read the immutable booking snapshot (§2.9), never current master data. Rule evaluation and the ship-modal estimate run **before** the freeze, on the working values that become that snapshot unchanged — so what was evaluated and what was frozen are the same values (**A1-03**, **A1-05**, **RV-05**).
- **INV-9 · COD conservation.** For any Order, `Σ collectible over Shipments with an active AWB` **never exceeds** F-15 order COD outstanding, and **equals** it while at least one Shipment on the Order holds an active AWB and `cod_assignment_state = ASSIGNED`. A shortfall while any Shipment is booked sets `cod_assignment_state = UNASSIGNED` (§3.24) and is surfaced, never tolerated silently. Before an Order's first booking the sum is legitimately 0. Enforced on the **order** key inside the booking transaction (**A3-01**, **A4-01**, **RV-03**).
- **INV-10 · Snapshot immutability.** `shipment.snapshot` is written once — at the `DRAFT → QUEUED` transition defined in §2.9 — and never modified thereafter. A new attempt on the same Shipment freezes a new snapshot on its own `DRAFT → QUEUED`; it never edits the old one (**RV-05**).
- **INV-11 · Sealed versions.** A `rate_card_version` (with its slabs and components), `commercial_zone_map` or `service_version` referenced by any booking snapshot is sealed: it cannot be edited or deleted, and backdating a new version never reprices an existing Shipment (**A1-05**).
- **INV-12 · Entitlement ledger.** Append-only and separate from Shopify charge records. Exactly one `DEBIT` per durably-confirmed non-test AWB; at most one `REVERSAL`, and only after courier-confirmed cancellation before any pickup event (**A1-04**).
- **INV-13 · Invoice numbering.** Numbers are allocated atomically per `(shop_id, gstin, financial_year, series_code)`, are never reused, and gaps are retained for voids only (**A1-08**, **A2-07**).
- **INV-14 · Import idempotency.** A re-uploaded reconciliation file with the same `content_hash` for the same Shop is a no-op, not a duplicate batch (**A1-06**).
- **INV-15 · Rounding locus.** Every money component is rounded half-up to paise when computed; totals are sums of stored rounded components (**A1-05**).
- **INV-16 · Correction pattern.** Immutable financial and issued-document facts are corrected only by cancellation, reversal, adjustment or a new linked version — never by editing the original (**A1-08**).
- **INV-17 · Terminal states.** A terminal state in any §3 machine is never silently regressed by a late event; the event is stored, shown and flagged for review (**A1-10**).
- **INV-18 · Secret confinement.** Plaintext credentials exist only inside the relevant adapter worker at call time. They never enter logs, queues, error payloads, admin or support views, analytics, or any export (**A1-12**).
- **INV-19 · Test isolation — both directions** (**A4-04**, **RV-08**). `shipment.is_test` is set from the courier account's `mode` at booking and is immutable thereafter, including when the account later switches to `LIVE`.
  **Excluded:** every rollup, dashboard figure, report, export, performance metric, COD expectation, freight and COD reconciliation row, entitlement debit, usage record, capacity figure (§5.1), **every write to Shopify** (no fulfillment, tracking number, fulfillment event, order tag or customer notification) and **every GST invoice**.
  **Not excluded — a test Shipment exercises the real path:** booking and the exactly-once protocol, label generation, pickup scheduling, cancellation, tracking ingestion by webhook and by polling, the full raw and normalized timeline, and NDR actions all behave **identically** to a live Shipment, so the onboarding wizard's step-5 test booking (§9.1.3) proves the integration. Any behaviour not in the excluded list is included.
  Test Shipments are **visually marked** wherever they appear in lists and detail views and are **filterable** (§9.23), and they and their child records carry the §5.3 append-only carve-out.
- **INV-20 · No silent drops.** Every unmatched, unmapped, unparseable or unexpected item — a raw status with no mapping, an AWB with no Shipment, an invoice charge type with no map, a fulfillment order that cannot be booked, a Shipment line with no resolvable weight, a late event after a terminal state — is surfaced for review. Nothing is discarded quietly.
- **INV-21 · Notifications never gate.** No booking, state transition or job outcome depends on the successful delivery of an email or any other notification (**A2-09**).
- **INV-22 · Optimistic concurrency.** Every write to a mutable `order`, `rule`, unsealed `rate_card_version`, `ticket`, reconciliation row, `DRAFT` shipment's working values or settings row carries the `version` the writer read (§2). A version mismatch **rejects** the write and returns the current state for the actor to refresh and reapply — never a silent last-write-wins merge (**A1-10**). The tracking reducer (§3.4) uses the same check.
- **INV-23 · The BYOC money boundary** (**RV-01**). Jsyxi **never adds a margin** to any courier rate: every price quoted, estimated, compared, displayed or reconciled is the merchant's own contracted price, and no field anywhere in the system marks one up. Jsyxi **holds no merchant balance, wallet, float or escrow** of any kind. **COD cash moves only between the courier and the merchant** — Jsyxi records and reconciles it (§9.17.3) and never receives, holds or disburses it; there is no payout, settlement or transfer action in the product. The **only** money Jsyxi charges a merchant is the Shopify Billing subscription plus AWB overage (§9.14). Any feature that would require otherwise is out of scope and is a change to the product's regulatory posture, not a design decision.
- **INV-24 · Exactly one default package profile.** Each Shop has exactly one `package_profile` row with `is_default = true`, seeded at onboarding (§5.6) and enforced by a unique partial index on `(shop_id) WHERE is_default`. It cannot be deleted, only replaced by promoting another profile in the same transaction. Without it F-20's last rung is non-deterministic and INV-7's dimension block can fail (**RW-21**).
